name: LM7815CT_NOPB
title: LM340, LM340A, LM7805, LM7812, LM7815: 1.5 A fixed positive voltage regulators, 5, 12 and 15 V
summary: Three-terminal linear regulators for fixed positive rails of 5, 12 or 15 V, good for 1.5 A and more with heat sinking, from inputs up to 35 V. Each has an internal current limit, over-temperature shutdown and output-transistor safe-area protection, and stays stable with nothing on its output. LM340A is a tighter 5 V grade. LM7815CT/NOPB is the 15 V part in a 3-pin TO-220.

Allowed dissipation at any ambient: PDMAX = (TJMAX − TA)/θJA, with TJMAX = 125°C or 150°C. Past it the die runs hotter than TJMAX and the electrical figures no longer hold; above 150°C the part shuts down thermally.
TO-3 (NDS): θJA 39°C/W; θJC 4°C/W, to which a heat sink's case-to-ambient resistance is added. TO-220 (NDE): θJA 54°C/W, θJC 4°C/W. SOT-223: θJA 174°C/W, lowered by heat sinking.
DDPAK/TO-263: θJA falls with PCB copper area tied to the tab: 50°C/W at 0.5 square inch, 37°C/W at 1 square inch, 32°C/W at 1.6 square inches or more.

circuits.title: Fixed output voltage regulator
circuits.description: The basic connection: input to INPUT, load on OUTPUT, GND to ground. C1, 0.22 µF across the input, is needed only when the regulator sits far from the supply's filter capacitor. C2 across the output is not needed for stability; it improves response to load steps, and 0.1 µF ceramic disc is the value given for it. The output voltage is the one fixed by the part number.

parts.note: needed when the regulator is far from the supply filter
ceramic disc; optional, for transient response

circuits.title: Input short protection
circuits.description: Protection for an input shorted to ground (S1) while a large capacitor holds the output up. D1, from OUTPUT to INPUT, carries the output capacitor's discharge around the regulator so it does not flow back through the chip. With 10 µF or less on the output the diode is generally not needed.

circuits.title: Current regulator
circuits.description: The regulator's fixed voltage, from OUTPUT to GND, is held across R1, so a set current flows through R1 and out of the GND-pin node into the load. The output current is that voltage over R1 plus the quiescent current, which shifts by 1.3 mA as line and load change. C1, 0.22 µF, bypasses the input.

circuits.title: Adjustable output regulator
circuits.description: The GND pin is lifted off ground by R2, a variable resistor with its wiper tied to its grounded end. R1 across OUTPUT to GND pin carries a fixed current (5 V over R1 for the 5 V part) which, with the quiescent current, flows through R2 and raises the output above the fixed voltage. C1, 0.22 µF, bypasses the input.

parts.note: variable; wiper tied to the ground end

circuits.title: High input voltage circuit with series resistor
circuits.description: A resistor in series with the input drops part of a high supply before the regulator, taking that share of the dissipation off the part. 0.22 µF bypasses the regulator input and 0.1 µF the output.

circuits.title: High input voltage circuit with transistor
circuits.description: An NPN transistor in series with the input takes up part of a high supply voltage. Its collector is on the supply and its emitter feeds the regulator input; a zener from the supply to the base and a resistor from emitter to base set the voltage it drops. 0.22 µF bypasses the regulator input and 0.1 µF the output.

circuits.title: High current voltage regulator
circuits.description: A PNP pass transistor, 2N6133, carries most of the load current alongside the regulator. The regulator's input current flows through R1, 3.0 Ω, from the supply; once the drop across R1 reaches the transistor's base-emitter voltage, Q1 turns on and feeds the output directly. 0.22 µF bypasses the regulator input and 0.1 µF the output.

circuits.title: High output current with short-circuit protection
circuits.description: The high-current circuit with a current limit on the pass transistor. Q1, 2N6132, takes the load current through RSC; when the drop across RSC turns Q2, 2N6124, on, Q2 feeds current from IN into Q1's base and limits Q1's current. R1, 3.0 Ω, carries the regulator's own input current and drives Q1's base. 0.22 µF bypasses the regulator input and 0.1 µF the output.

parts.note: current sense, sets the short-circuit current

circuits.title: LM340 used with negative regulator LM79xx
circuits.description: A dual supply from one transformer with two centre-tapped secondaries. Each secondary feeds a two-diode full-wave rectifier and a reservoir capacitor; the LM340 regulates the upper rectifier into +OUT and an LM79xx regulates the lower into -OUT, about the common ground. Each output carries 0.1 µF and a diode, D5 from ground to +OUT and D6 from -OUT to ground.

operation.text: Monolithic three-terminal positive regulators with fixed outputs of 5 V, 12 V and 15 V. They take up to 35 V in and, with enough heat sinking, deliver more than 1.5 A. LM340A is the higher-accuracy 5 V version, ±2% at TJ = 25°C, with tighter line and load regulation. With external parts the same chips make adjustable voltage or current sources. LM7815CT/NOPB is the 15 V part in TO-220.

Built in: a current limit, shutdown on over-temperature and safe-operating-area protection of the output transistor. The typical current limit is 2.4 A. Thermal shutdown acts when the junction reaches 150°C. The part has no operating modes beyond regulating.
Current beyond 1.5 A is available; how much is set by the package and the heat sink, since a lower effective θJA lets the part dissipate more power.

The part is stable without any output capacitor; 0.1 µF ceramic on the output improves transient response. A 0.22 µF input capacitor is needed only when the regulator is far from the supply filter capacitor: beyond 6 inches it needs 0.1 µF or more across the input, any kind of capacitor, to stay stable. Both are placed as near the regulator as possible.
Input up to 35 V. Minimum input for line and load regulation at TJ = 25°C: 7.5 V for the 5 V parts, 14.6 V for 12 V, 17.7 V for 15 V (IO ≤ 1 A).

With a large output capacitor, a short of the input to ground leaves the output charged while the input falls; the capacitor then dumps its charge back into the chip through an internal diode from input to output and stray transistors, which can destroy the part. A fast diode from output to input diverts that current. At 10 µF of output capacitance or less it is generally not needed.
The output cannot sink current. Forcing it above the input damages internal low-current paths in the same way as an input short.

With only the GND pin disconnected, the output rises towards the unregulated input and can damage the load. Reconnecting ground with power on can damage the regulator. The case to watch is plugging regulators, or boards carrying them, into live sockets: switch power off first, or make ground connect first.

An input transient above the maximum rated input voltage, or more than 0.8 V below ground, damages the regulator if it carries enough energy. Protection against them: a big capacitor on the input, a breakdown diode in series with the input, an inductor, a suppressor device, alone or together.

Once the needed sink-to-ambient resistance θ(H–A) is worked out, the heat sink chosen must have a θ(H–A) at or below it. Heat sink makers give θ(H–A) as a number or as a curve of temperature rise against dissipated power.

Load-current traces are wide to keep their inductance low. A bypass capacitor right at the OUTPUT pin improves PSRR. Example placement for DDPAK and SOT-223: C1 at the input lead and C2 at the output lead, side by side just below the leads, with the ground lead between them running to ground copper.

Both use board copper and the board itself as the heat sink, with the tab soldered to the copper plane. The DDPAK curve of θJA against area is measured on 1 oz copper with no solder mask over the heat-sinking area. Above 1 square inch more copper helps very little, and the lowest θJA reached for DDPAK on a board is 32°C/W. Its dissipation curve assumes θJA = 35°C/W and TJMAX = 125°C. The SOT-223 dissipation curves assume θJA = 74°C/W on 1 oz copper and 51°C/W on 2 oz copper, with TJMAX = 125°C.
Built-in ESD protection is limited. Store and handle the parts with leads shorted together or in conductive foam.
